newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yeltsin confirms NATO-Russia deal set for Paris.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin confirms NATO-Russia deal set for Paris.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Thursday Moscow would sign an agreement with NATO at their Paris summit on May 27 about the alliance's planned expansion into Eastern Europe.

"We want to announce...that on the 27th of May in Paris the agreement will be signed by the leaders of the NATO countries and of Russia," he told a news conference after talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl
"So we need to hurry," he added.

Russian demands that NATO agree to limit the stationing of foreign troops in East European countries that join the alliance have held up preparations for the summit. NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Wednesday the negotiations might not be finished in time for the Paris meeting.
Kohl said the document was mostly finished but some parts needed more work urgently. He and Yeltsin declined to give any details.
